title: The New Job Market: Hiring, Hunting, and AI in the Middle
description:
This session looks at how AI is reshaping every stage of the job hunt - from the CV that gets written, to the screening system that reads it, to the interview on the other side, to the market candidates are landing in.

The focus is practical and aimed at job seekers, career changers, and anyone trying to make sense of how hiring actually works now - but recruiters, hiring managers, and HR folks will get plenty out of it too.

We'll explore-

* The current challenges, specifically in the Auckland NZ marketplace
* Writing CVs and cover letters with AI - what works, what flags as generic, and how to keep your voice
* Getting past the bots - how applicant tracking systems and AI screeners actually evaluate applications
* The new interview landscape - AI-assisted screening calls, async video interviews, and live AI note-takers
* Interview prep with AI - mock interviews, company research, and rehearsing tough questions
* Where AI helps you stand out vs. where it makes everyone sound the same
* Job market shifts - which roles are growing, shrinking, or changing shape, and what that means for positioning
* Building an AI-resilient career - skills, signals, and portfolios that hold their value
* Spotting fake jobs, scam recruiters, and AI-generated postings
* Practical workflows and tools that are actually worth using

After these sessions we typically grab dinner nearby if you want to keep the conversation going and connect with other professionals.

title: Come Together - Bruce Springstein
location: The Civic, Corner of Queen Street and Wellesley Street West, Auckland City Centre, Auckland, Auckland
description:
New Zealand’s most successful rock series ever, Come Together, returns in 2026 with an electrifying trio of landmark albums: Bruce Springsteen’s Born to Run, Radiohead’s OK Computer and Talking Heads’ Stop Making Sense.
Each album will be performed live, in full, by a rotating supergroup of Aotearoa’s most acclaimed rock artists and musicians - followed by a second set of classics and deep cuts that span each artist’s extraordinary catalogue.
From the wall of sound production of Born to Run, to the haunting dystopian brilliance of OK Computer, to the joyful and immersive perfection of Stop Making Sense - the 2026 series celebrates three albums that have cemented their place in music history. Performed in some of the country’s most beautiful venues, Come Together once again promises epic musicianship, emotional punch and the kind of once-in-a-lifetime collaborations that have made the series a cultural phenomenon.
The album that transformed Bruce Springsteen from a struggling artist on the brink of being dropped to a full-blown rock star, Born to Run remains one of the defining records of the 1970s. Sweeping, cinematic and bursting with heart, it delivered immortal tracks including Thunder Road, Born to Run and the epic Jungleland.
Come Together will perform the album in its entirety, followed by a second set diving deep into Springsteen’s vast catalogue - from anthems to hidden gems.
Performed by: Milan Borich, Adam McGrath, Jennie Skulander, Jon Toogood and the Come Together band.

title: Sit & Think: How We Actually Learn (After the Walk)
description:
You know the moment. The walk is winding down, the conversation has just hit something good, and then everyone drifts off to the carpark.

This is for that conversation.

Here is a thought I keep coming back to. We spend our childhoods being taught: sat in rows, told what to know, tested on whether we kept it. Then we grow up, and the real learning quietly moves somewhere else. It starts happening in conversations, in disagreements, in the things experience teaches us, and in the moments we change our minds over a drink.

There is even a word for it: *andragogy*, the art of helping adults learn. The idea is that adults learn best not when they are lectured at, but when their own experience is in the room and they get to think things through alongside other people. Which is more or less what a good walk, and a good pint afterwards, already are.

So this first session turns that idea on itself. We will sit with a deceptively simple question: how do adults actually learn, and when did you last genuinely change your mind about something that mattered?

Here is how it runs. I open with a short talk, about ten minutes, to set the question up, not to settle it. Then the floor is yours. It is an open, facilitated discussion, which is a fancy way of saying I keep things moving and make sure everyone who wants to speak gets the room to. Your experience is the material. Bring it, along with your half-formed hunches and your disagreements. Especially the disagreements, kept warm of course.

No prep, no reading, nothing to know in advance.

**📅 When:** Saturday 6 June, straight after the walk. We will get started around 3:15 PM, once everyone has a drink in hand.
**📍 Where:** Orakei Local Bar & Kitchen, 228 Orakei Road, Remuera (where the walk finishes)

title: No Other Land (2024) Palestine
description:
No Other Land is a documentary/drama about life in Palestine. This is the second in our films about Palestine. The intention here is to open up discussion based on the power of cinema to portray the lives of ordinary people in their struggles in the face of oppressive forces.

We know the debate about whether the films of Leni Riefenstahl in WW2 were propaganda or art. Great cinema paints a picture of people whose lives become real in front of our eyes. We are forced to make decisions as to to whom we relate and what we will do.

"A combination of hand-held footage and intimate scenes of ordinary Palestinian life among extraordinary instability are woven together at an artful pace. Not one of the 95 minutes feels wasted. Given the work that Adra and Abraham do during years of filming to record and share the truth, this is a film that asks, both out-loud and implicitly: if people knew, would things change? *No Other Land* is both an invitation and a wero, a generous offering that demands to be seen and discussed. — Nadia Abu-Shanab." (reviewer for the NZ International Film Festival)

Biography:
Emily Lyall of Te Whakatōhea and Te Whānau-a-Apanui is interested in exploring alternative modes of curation and exhibition making, approaching her practice with an Indigenous lens.
Her studies in Māori Visual Arts, Toioho ki Āpiti and Museum and Heritage Practice, Te Herenga Waka inform her passion for arts engagement and culture. Some of her recent work includes exhibiting at Te Manawa, curating for Toi Māori Aotearoa and interning at Te Papa Tongarewa in kaitiakitanga taonga Māori and education.

title: Arbor Day planting
location: Clark Street Common, Wolverton Street, New Lynn, Auckland, Auckland
description:
Nau mai, haere mai!
We're celebrating Arbor Day by getting trees into the ground and we'd love to for you to join us there.
Come along to plant native plants on the banks of the Waitahurangi Awa in New Lynn and bring it one step closer to becoming a thriving habitat for native birds and fish.
It's a challenging site, so a reasonable standard of fitness is required. You'll need to wear gumboots or sturdy closed shoes. Please bring a rain jacket and gardening gloves if you have any.
After our mahi we will finish with a BBQ.
This event is a collaboration between EcoMatters, the Tree Council, the New Zealand Arboricultural Association (NZ ARB) and supported by the Whau Local Board & Whau Wildlink.

title: Kids learn to ride
description:
Learning to ride a bike is one of those big childhood milestones and being part of that experience as a parent or caregiver is a thrill.
Whether they're starting on a balance bike or making the transition to pedals, this course will teach kids aged 2–13 years old how to ride a bike.
All our Kids learn to ride courses are:

Free
Drop-in (no registration required)
Led by highly qualified instructors
A great way to increase confidence and skills
An opportunity to learn tips and tricks to practice with your kids at home.

Sessions run on a drop-in basis. Bring your own bike or try one of ours.
